BiblicalUsage: Rachuwm means compassionate — it is the name God gives Himself. When He passed before Moses He proclaimed, 'The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth'; Joel says, 'rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful'; and Jonah confesses he fled because he knew God is 'gracious, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness.'
TheologicalSignificance: This tells me that this word is the heart of the whole Bible: God is compassionate first, before He is anything else to us, and every other attribute bends toward mercy. And I hold that Jonah's complaint proves it — he was angry precisely because God was merciful, and God was merciful anyway.
